title: Best Open-Source Agent Builder Tools to Watch in 2026
summary: A practical shortlist of LiteLLM, Langfuse, promptfoo, Ragas, MCP Inspector, and MCP SDKs for teams building agent products.
author: OpenAgent.bot Editors
seoTitle: Best Open-Source Agent Builder Tools to Watch in 2026
seoDescription: Compare LiteLLM, Langfuse, promptfoo, Ragas, MCP Inspector, FastMCP, and MCP SDKs for building AI agent products.
body: The best agent builder stack is not one framework. It is a small set of layers: a model gateway, traces, evaluations, tool connectors, and a repeatable way to test changes before an agent reaches real users.

For a practical 2026 shortlist, start with **LiteLLM** for model routing, **Langfuse** for observability, **promptfoo** for prompt and agent tests, **Ragas** for RAG quality checks, and **MCP Inspector** or MCP SDKs when the agent needs tool connectors.
## Quick recommendation
- Use [LiteLLM](/tools/litellm) when your agent needs provider routing, gateway logs, or OpenAI-compatible access to many model APIs.
- Use [Langfuse](/tools/langfuse) when you need traces, prompt versions, datasets, and production feedback loops.
- Use [promptfoo](/tools/promptfoo) when you need repeatable tests for prompts, agents, RAG systems, or red-team checks.
- Use [Ragas](/tools/ragas) when your agent depends on retrieval quality or RAG-style context.
- Use [MCP Inspector](/tools/mcp-inspector) and the [MCP Python SDK](/plugins/model-context-protocol-python-sdk) when you need to expose tools and data through Model Context Protocol.
## Comparison table
| Tool | Layer | Best first test | Official source |
| [LiteLLM](/tools/litellm) | Model gateway | Route two providers through one proxy and compare cost/logs | [GitHub](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm) |
| [Langfuse](/tools/langfuse) | Observability | Trace one agent workflow end to end | [GitHub](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse) |
| [promptfoo](/tools/promptfoo) | Testing and red teaming | Turn ten prompts or agent tasks into a repeatable eval | [GitHub](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo) |
| [Ragas](/tools/ragas) | RAG evaluation | Evaluate retrieval/context quality on one dataset | [GitHub](https://github.com/vibrantlabsai/ragas) |
| [MCP Inspector](/tools/mcp-inspector) | Connector debugging | Inspect one MCP server before connecting it to an agent | [GitHub](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector) |
## What to add first
If your product is still a prototype, add tests before adding dashboards. A small promptfoo suite can reveal regressions faster than a large observability setup.
If your product already has users, add traces and datasets. Langfuse becomes more useful once you can connect real production failures to prompts, model calls, and evaluation examples.
If your agent calls many providers, add a gateway early. LiteLLM is useful when cost, routing, and fallback behavior become part of the product architecture.
If your agent needs external tools, evaluate MCP as a connector layer. MCP Inspector and the official SDKs help you validate tool behavior before giving the agent access.
